newsitem.title: FRANCE: BA calls news conference on Air Liberte.
newsitem.headline: BA calls news conference on Air Liberte.

text.p: British Airways' French subsidiary TAT called a news conference on Wednesday to announce "an important development" in the bidding for ailing airline Air Liberte but refused to give nore details.
TAT chairman March Rochet will hold the news conference at 1500 GMT in a Paris hotel.

A spokeswoman for Nouvelles Frontieres chairman Jacques Maillot, who heads a French/Moroccan consortium also bidding for Air Liberte, had no comment on reports he gave financial details to the Creteil commercial court on Wednesday.
A spokeswoman at the Creteil commercial court said there was no sign yet that a decision on the future of Air Liberte could be imminent.
Sources at the Air Liberte works council do not expect a decision before Friday or Monday.
Air Liberte went into administration on September 26 with debts of about 1.5 billion francs.
British Airways, Richard Branson's Brussels-based Virgin Express, a consortium headed Jacques Maillot, and commercial pilot Fernand Denan have made offers for Air Liberte.

British Airways plans to pay 25 million francs for Air Liberte and aims to merge it with its French TAT. The British airline said on Friday it had plans to spend 440 million francs on getting Air Liberte back into profit in three years.

Air Liberte owns about a quarter of the landing and take-off slots at Orly airport, Paris' second airport specialising in domestic flights, and this would dramatically boost BA's presence and competitiveness in France.
Air Liberte lost 650 million francs in the first nine months of 1996 due to an air fare war and insufficient passenger numbers.

Since the start of the year the main French domestic routes are open to competition ahead of full liberalistaion in 1997. Air Liberte and other regional group AOM have been fighting to take market share from former monopolist Air Inter, part of Air France.
Jacques Maillot, also chairman of smaller airline Corsair, counts the Rivaud bank, travel group Club Mediterranee and Royal Air Maroc in his consortium.
